identity.rationale: Zapier's strict all-assertions pass rate on the private split. Distinct from Artificial Analysis's objective-and-guardrail re-score of the same tasks.

task: Complete cross-app business workflows in a simulated company by discovering and calling REST APIs. Grading reads the final environment state.
metric: Mean of task_completed_correctly: 1 only when every assertion passes, else 0, reported as a percent.
protocol: Zapier dataset 1.0.6 private split, toolset api, one attempt, 50-step cap, no LLM judge. Effort is the level printed on the row. A fallback label means another model answered some tasks, so that row is not one model alone.

usefulness.rationale: On the 1.0.6 private board read 2026-09-23, strict pass rates still sit far below 100% and separate a current frontier Max row from a current open Max row. GPT 6 Astra (Max) scores 41.4% with no fallback label. DeepSeek V4 Flash (Max) scores 18.11% with no fallback label. GLM-5.3 is not on this board. Kimi K3 scores 22.68% and its weights are published, but that private row prints no effort, so it is not in this pair. The 42.47% leader is a default-fallback run and is not used as the frontier result.

results.configuration: Zapier private leaderboard, dataset 1.0.6, toolset api, metric task_completed_correctly. Labels on the shared pair: GPT 6 Astra (Max), effort Max, no fallback annotation; DeepSeek V4 Flash (Max), effort Max, no fallback annotation, cost cell marked with the Fireworks cached-rate footnote. Each row uses that model's own Max effort, not matched compute. Fallback contamination: neither row is a fallback run. The 42.47% leader, Claude Opus 5.5 (default fallbacks, Max), is excluded because Zapier says refused tasks were rerun on the provider's fallback model.

review.rationale: Primary-source review verified both Zapier rows: GPT-6 Astra (Max) at 41.4% and DeepSeek V4 Flash (Max) at 18.11%, on AutomationBench 1.0.6, API toolset, with no fallback annotation; both are percent strict pass rates and both are dated by observation on 2026-09-23. The rows share benchmark version, configuration and unit, and their model IDs are present in the agentic reference set as a closed frontier model and an open-weight model from different organizations. The page documents the task, metric, protocol and usefulness, and the benchmark is distinct from automationbench_aa because it reports Zapier's strict all-assertions pass rate rather than AA's objective-and-guardrail re-score. The fallback leader and the effortless Kimi row were correctly excluded. The cited primary sources also support that DeepSeek V4 Flash is a current DeepSeek model and open-weight; open-weight is not treated as open-source.
